subject: Request: Executive sign-off for PS bundle & custom integration waiver
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Emma Gonzalez <emma.gonzalez@luminahealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: PS bundle proposal + custom integration scope (follow-up)

Hi Emma —

Great meeting this morning. Per our conversation I attached a revised SOW that includes the premium onboarding package (4-week white-glove), two dedicated integration sprints to connect your single-sign-on + EHR mapping, and a 12-month Premium Support plan.

High-level commercial ask: Lumina is asking for a 20% one-time discount on services and a waiver on our standard integration clause that normally requires an additional change-order for mapping beyond 2 endpoints. They need the waiver to cover the EHR mapping work listed in section 3.2 in the SOW so they can commit to an aggressive Q3 go-live.

Attachments: SOW_Lumina_v2.pdf, PricingBreakdown.xlsx, Redwood_Security_Addendum.pdf

If possible, I want to close pricing this week. I need an executive sign-off on the discount and the limited scope waiver. I'm escalating to Deal Desk / Sales Ops at Redwood to request approval.

Proposed commercial: $320,000 services list -> with 20% discount = $256,000 (requested).
Fallback we can accept: 15% discount + onboarding credit of $25k.

Thanks —
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0189
From: Emma Gonzalez <emma.gonzalez@luminahealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@luminahealth.com
Date: 2027-04-12T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PS bundle proposal + custom integration scope (follow-up)

Rafael —

Thanks for sending this over. Procurement will need final numbers and a statement of work that isolates the EHR mapping deliverables. A few quick questions: what is the committed go-live date with the proposed approach, and can Redwood provide a one-page acceptance criteria list for integration?

We do have internal constraints on capital spend this quarter, so the 20% helps, but procurement will push back if there are open scope waivers without clear limits. If you can get exec sign-off on a single waiver that lists exact endpoints and a hard cap of 40 hours for out-of-scope changes, procurement will be comfortable moving to PO.

Emma Gonzalez
Director, Digital Programs | Lumina Health
emma.gonzalez@luminahealth.com
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-12T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: PS bundle proposal + custom integration scope — executive approval request

Folks — forwarding Lumina's reply and the SOW/pricing. TL;DR: Customer asks for 20% one-time services discount + a waiver to our integration change-order that would cover EHR mapping (they want 3 endpoints covered). Procurement will only accept if waiver includes hard caps and acceptance criteria.

Why we should consider: Strategic healthcare account, logos + reference potential across their network; they commit to 12-month Premium Support and a 3x subscription expansion target in year 2. Revenue footprint if expanded is large.

Risks: custom mapping increases delivery complexity; if we under-resource the integration it could impact go-live and cause churn. Legal will need to sign the waiver.

Requested approvals: (1) one-time 20% discount on services, (2) temporary scope waiver to include the 3 EHR endpoints in base SOW with a 40-hour hard cap on additional mapping, (3) approval to expedite DocuSign and start work upon PO receipt.

Attachments (again): SOW_Lumina_v2.pdf; PricingBreakdown.xlsx; Redwood_Security_Addendum.pdf

Please advise — Rafael
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-12T13:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: PS bundle proposal + custom integration scope — executive approval request

Rafael — thanks for the context and SOW. A few notes:

- Can we tighten the waiver language to enumerate the exact 3 endpoints (Auth, PatientLookup, Results) and explicitly state the 40-hour cap? That will satisfy procurement and limit our exposure.
- I'm comfortable moving up to a 15% discount without further escalations, provided we offer a $25k onboarding credit instead of 20% off (keeps list price integrity).
- Legal review required for the waiver and acceptance criteria — please loop legal early (cc'd laura).

If Lumina insists on 20% we should request an expansion commitment (written target of X seats/instances in 12 months) or a phased payment schedule that ties acceptance to milestone payments.

Monica Patel
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-12T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: PS bundle proposal + custom integration scope — executive approval request

Team — after reading the SOW and risk notes I approve the following on an exception basis:

1) Approve a one-time commercial concession equivalent to a 15% discount AND a $25,000 onboarding credit (combined concession).
2) Approve the limited scope waiver to include the three named endpoints (Auth, PatientLookup, Results) in the base SOW provided the waiver text includes a 40-hour cap and explicit acceptance criteria for each endpoint.
3) Legal (Laura) to review and sign off on waiver language. Procurement must sign the acceptance criteria page before PO.
4) Delivery to reserve a small buffer (one engineer for 2 weeks) to protect the go-live date — any additional hours beyond the 40-hr cap will be billed per change-order rates.

Rafael — please update the SOW with the tightened waiver language, the onboarding credit, and send the DocuSign package to Lumina and procurement. Once legal signs off, finance can accept PO and we will begin work upon receipt.

Marissa Cole
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
[Approved — exec sign-off provided 2027-04-12 16:45 PDT]
